narrative: A 24-year-old journalist from Ras al-Ein, in northwest Syria near the Turkish border, was captured and imprisoned by ISIS in 2013 while trying to make a film in Raqqa. He was held for a month, first in a tiny closet cell standing with three others for 12 hours in darkness, then questioned as a suspected spy, beaten with a cable, and threatened with execution or transfer to a military court in Mosul. He was released only through the intervention of local clans who negotiated on his behalf. His father warned him not to return home; he was wanted by the regime and other parties for his journalism. In July 2013 he crossed into Turkey, first to the French embassy in Ankara to be questioned about kidnapped French journalists, then to Istanbul, where work was scarce and employers discriminated against Syrians. He moved to Gaziantep to work as a photographer for the exiled Syrian interim government, a role he eventually left. His family was forced from their homes by Kurdish forces because of his work, and fled to Turkey; he met them in Urfa and, at 22, became responsible for them all. He freelanced for foreign news organizations, was robbed in Istanbul, and married his fiancee, whom he had met online while she was in Iraq. In the spring he planned the trip to Europe for a month with his cousin, then traveled with a large group to Izmir on the Aegean coast to board a boat for Greece. His wife followed separately four months later. He received a three-year residence permit and now lives in Berlin, studying art and photography.
